Fails Info Contains personal notes covering each component and my research considerations. You'll also find wiring diagrams and notes on related tools/parts that are not part of the build itself.
https://www.amd.com/en/products/processors/desktops/ryzen/9000-series/amd-ryzen-9-9950x3d.html Delidded for better temps and a fun challenge Ordered tray version due to warranty being voided by delidding anyway Best performing consumer CPU in 2025
TG Ryzen 7000 Delid-Die-Mate was used for the delid

https://www.corsair.com/de/en/p/memory/cmk96gx5m2b6000z30/vengeance-96gb-2x48gb-ddr5-dram-6000mts-cl30-amd-expo-intel-xmp-memory-kit-cmk96gx5m2b6000z30 96gb at 6000MT/s with 30-36-36-76 timings should last me a long time
https://rog.asus.com/graphics-cards/graphics-cards/rog-astral/rog-astral-rtx5090-o32g-gaming/ Per-pin-monitoring support
Fits the TG DeltaMate GPU Block Astral block Best performing consumer GPU in 2025

https://www.kingston.com/en/ssd/gaming/kingston-fury-renegade-g5-nvme-m2-ssd SM2508, low temperature gen 5 drive High TBW rating Crazy IOPS due to gen 5 Crucial T705/T710 Samsung 9100 Pro WD_Black SN8100
https://rog.asus.com/motherboards/rog-strix/rog-strix-x870-i-gaming-wifi/ Good connectivity
Fits Jonsbo D31 Mesh Screen and provides space on the bottom/right side of the case for accessories and cable management Active cooling for VRM and SSD/Chipset
https://rog.asus.com/power-supply-units/rog-loki/rog-loki-1200t-sfx-l-gaming-model/ Short enough to fit cables/tubing beneath the PSU interface
Clearance for reservoir mounting screws on the grill side because of the Jonsbo D31 Mesh Screen's ATX sized PSU cage Titanium cert and more than enough power for the system
https://www.thermal-grizzly.com/en/amd-mycro-direct-die-pro/s-tg-my-dd-p-amd
Only available direct die block for Ryzen 9 9950x3D Optimus Signature V3 Pro: annoying to get and expensive to import + I couldnt find official direct die contact frames
https://www.thermal-grizzly.com/en/deltamate-gpu-block-astral/s-tg-dm-gpu In-/Outlets are positioned perfectly for the loop Good design and material quality
https://www.thermal-grizzly.com/en/products/fittings-terminals/ Minimalistic, black, high quality, low profile and small fittings
https://shop.alphacool.com/en/shop/radiators/360mm/rad-alphacool-nexxxos-hpe-30-full-copper-360mm-radiator Systems drain port is as low as possible due to the drain port on the rad Simple black design with white logos Full copper
I've guessed 18fpi 30mm to be the best for sufficient intake airflow with Noctua NF-A12x25 G2
I've chosen 30mm rad thickness to leave some space below the TG DeltaMate GPU Block Astral for airflow
2.5cm clearance between the fans on the rad and TG DeltaMate GPU Block Astral Thermaltake Pacific CLD 360 25fpi, 40mm: too thick for sufficient clearance & fpi probably too high for pull intake Thermaltake Pacific CLM 360 14fpi, 40mm: too thick for sufficient clearance & fpi probably too low to handle CPU/GPU loads Watercool Heatkiller RAD 360-S 14-15fpi, 30mm: no drain port & didn't like the stainless steel endcap aesthetic EK-Quantum Surface P360M 18fpi, 44mm: too thick & didn't like the stainless steel endcap aesthetic
https://stealkeycustoms.de/en/products/sc-respro-120-d5-ddc-d-rgb Pump positioned behind the reservoir -> no visible cables/pump chasis Is small enough to fit the case Awesome design
A hole was drilled into Jonsbo D31 Mesh Screen to offset the pump reservoir combo further back to make room for the In/Outlet fittings of the TG DeltaMate GPU Block Astral
Watercool UNI 120 Acryl: has a visible RGB strip
EK-Quantum Kinetic FLT 120: too many unused ports & every liquid cooled Jonsbo D31 Mesh Screen build I've seen uses it
https://shop.aquacomputer.de/Water-Cooling/Pumps-Accessories/Pumps/D5-NEXT-pump::3785.html I didn't consider drilling a hole into the case during research, therefore I chose pwm since vario pumps wouldn't be accesible after assembly
A hole was drilled into Jonsbo D31 Mesh Screen to offset the pump reservoir combo, more on that in Bitspower BP-120RADH-BK
Bought a second D5 for the MO-RA IV 400 Extension, the fan header on the D5 NEXT makes the setup really clean Aquasuite support Watercool WCP D5-Vario
https://shop.aquacomputer.de/Monitoring-and-Controlling/Sensors/Flow-sensor-high-flow-NEXT-G1-4::3953.html From my research the only accurate flow meter on the market Aquasuite support
https://shop.aquacomputer.de/Monitoring-and-Controlling/QUADRO-and-OCTO/OCTO-fan-controller-for-PWM-fans::3832.html Standalone fan/pump controller with temperature sensors Asus BIOS/background software independent pwm control Aquasuite support
https://shop.aquacomputer.de/USB-accessories/HUBBY7-internal-USB-2-0-Hub::3419.html
Not enough USB 2.0 headers on ROG STRIX X870-I GAMING WIFI Aquasuite support
https://shop.aquacomputer.de/Monitoring-and-Controlling/farbwerk-for-RGBpx/farbwerk-360::3798.html
Needed non-proprietary 5V ARGB headers for SC ResPro 120 D5 + TG DeltaMate GPU Block Astral + TG Mycro Direct-Die Pro Aquasuite support
https://shop.aquacomputer.de/Monitoring-and-Controlling/Sensors/Temperature-sensor-G1-4::3126.html
Aquasuite doesn't support linux and I want a software independant temperature readout for the fan curves of the Aqua Computer Octo
https://shop.aquacomputer.de/Water-Cooling/Coolant/Double-Protect-Ultra-5l-canister::3127.html Non-opaque liquid for low maintenance Thermal Grizzly uses it internally -> I'll be using it too
https://shop.aquacomputer.de/Water-Cooling/Fittings-Tubes/System-16-10-mm/Hose-Aqua-Computer-16-10-mm-EPDM-black::4069.html
Fits well with TG DeltaMate Fittings
https://www.ekwb.com/shop/ek-quantum-torque-drain-valve-satin-titanium Clean drain valve design
Screwed into a 14mm TG DeltaMate Fittings and mounted on the bottom Alphacool NexXxoS HPE-30 (18fpi)
A hole was drilled into Jonsbo D31 Mesh Screen to mount it I did a terrible job lining up the hole since I drilled the initial hole before owning a proper step drill set. That's why it looks so sketchy

Two Alphacool NexXxoS HPE-30 (18fpi) arent capable of handling gaming loads with a compact RTX 5090 Astral OC and Ryzen 9 9950x3D configuration at reasonable temps. I opted for the total overkill option to solve that.

https://shop.watercool.de/MO-RA-IV-400-Black_1 3.2 square meters aluminium surface and 38 meters of pipe? hell yeah
Aqua Computer D5 NEXT The fan header makes cable management really clean
https://shop.watercool.de/Noctua-NF-A20-HS-PWM-chromaxblack_1 They were spefically designed for MO-RAs I just needed "a" reservoir for mounting a second pump, there are nice Heatkiller mounting solutions for the MO-RA 150mm Tube, Multiport Top 2xG1/4, D5 Bottom Hub
https://shop.aquacomputer.de/Water-Cooling/Filters/Filter-with-stainless-steel-mesh-ball-valves-and-mounting-plate-G1-4::2421.html?language=en For less frequent maintenance For some reason the g1/4 threads are spaced so close to each other that no normal 16/10 fitting will fit
I used the very thin Bitspower 15mm Extender to make that happen
https://www.aquatuning.com/en/watercooling/custom-watercooling/fittings/adapters/bitspower-extension-g1/4-zoll-to-g1/4-zoll-15mm-matt-black
Used for the standalone adapter (see Koolance Quick Disconnect Fittings) and to make two TG DeltaMate Fittings fit next to each other for the Aquacomputer Filter
Sata: Phobya SATA Extension 60cm, used together with the ROG-LOKI-1200T-SFX-L stock SATA cable to get power from my PSU to the second pump
PWM: Phobya male to male 30cm and left over noctua NA-SEC1 cables to connect the fans to the pumps fan header
USB: Aqua Computer 53213, 2 meter usb cable used to connect the second Aqua Computer D5 NEXT
https://www.caseking.de/ek-water-blocks-ek-quantum-torque-pass-through-g1-4-schwarz/WAEK-2673.html
To cover up the holes and create mounting points for Koolance Quick Disconnect Fittings If Thermal Grizzlies pass-through fittings would have been released earlier, I would have went with them
Koolance QD3-MT10X16 / Koolance QD3-FT10X16 for the connecting tubes
Koolance QD3-MTG4 / Koolance QD3-FTG4 for a standalone adapter and direct mounting on the passthrough fittings

https://www.thermal-grizzly.com/en/conductonaut-extreme/s-tg-ce Works well
https://www.thermal-grizzly.com/en/conductonaut/s-tg-c-005-r Ordered 5g to disolve the soldering tin while delidding and future projects
https://www.thermal-grizzly.com/en/phasesheet-ptm/s-tg-ps No pump out, low maintenance I considered Kryosheet and liquid metal but the benefit/risk ratio wasn't worth it imo lol
https://www.thermal-grizzly.com/en/shield-coating/s-tg-ash
Unecessary due to factory protection, it makes my Ryzen 9 9950x3D SMDs look all fancy tho
https://www.jonsbo.com/en/products/D31meshfupingbanBlack.html Nice building challenge
A screen for AIDA64, its a non hdcp monitor which can lead to gpu driver crashes with heavy drm content
A ~68mm hole for SC ResPro 120 D5, a ~26mm hole for EK Torque Drain Valve and two holes for passthough fittings were drilled into the case using Step Drill Set and KWB Hole Saw
US: https://custom.cablemod.com/5cde38be7c5b
EU: https://custom.cablemod.com/686519e88695 Their noctua colors looked the best Needed custom length cables to make cable management somewhat enjoyable (it wasn't)
Had a 20% discount code from purchasing ROG-LOKI-1200T-SFX-L Added a third SATA connector for a potential 2.5" SSD at the back They sent me a broken Molex cable

https://noctua.at/en/nf-a12x25-g2-pwm Noctua color scheme <3 Good performing and quiet all-rounder Ordered Sx2-PP versions with offset speed for mitigating undesirable harmonic noise
The external intake fan at the back is for blowing air over the TG DeltaMate GPU Block Astral backplate and Vengeance 96GB 6000MT/s
https://www.thermal-grizzly.com/en/detail/0464bdf130ed41eab3aa218bba8b219e Live monitoring accurate GPU power consumption I'd replace it with the wireview pro 2 if they release an 180° version for peace of mind
https://www.amazon.de/dp/B0DQKC79F1?th=1
Supports the 2.1kg TG DeltaMate GPU Block Astral and can be screwed into the Alphacool NexXxoS HPE-30 (18fpi)

https://shop.aquacomputer.de/Monitoring-and-Controlling/Accessories/Connection-cable-alarm-header-with-miniature-connector-to-motherboard-power-switch-header::3488.html
Proprietary connector that connects the Aqua Computer high flow NEXT to one of the power button headers on the ROG STRIX X870-I GAMING WIFI turning the system off in case of insufficient liquid flow rate
https://www.amazon.de/dp/B097GZHR1J?th=1
Jonsbo D31 Mesh Screen doesn't have a dust filter on the back
https://www.thermal-grizzly.com/en/delid-die-mate/s-tg-ddm-r7000
Used to delid Ryzen 9 9950x3D
https://toom.de/p/stufenbohrer-set-4-32-mm-3-teilig/1752050
Used to drill a ~26mm hole into Jonsbo D31 Mesh Screen for EK Torque Drain Valve
Used to drill two holes for passthrough fittings for the MO-RA IV 400 Extension
https://toom.de/p/bimetall-lochsaege-68-mm/1752363
Used to drill a ~68mm hole into Jonsbo D31 Mesh Screen for SC ResPro 120 D5
https://www.ekwb.com/shop/ek-loop-leak-tester-flex Well
https://github.com/ChrisTitusTech/winutil Creating windows ISO images Configuring windows after install Makes Win11 a little more enjoyable
https://toom.de/p/zylinderschrauben-sl-schlitz-edelstahl-m4-x-16-mm-10-stueck/1651164
Used to mount SC ResPro 120 D5 to the PSU cage of the Jonsbo D31 Mesh Screen
https://www.amazon.de/dp/B000TFZ0LA?th=1
Used to decouple SC ResPro 120 D5 from the PSU cage (didnt do much I think, I dont have a control)
Vibrations in Jonsbo D31 Mesh Screen are probably pretty loud with the thin metal on metal PSU cage update: its still pretty loud

https://www.amazon.de/dp/B007N8SKK4
Used to mount SC ResPro 120 D5 on the PSU cage
Heavy modifications required to make the bottom bracket fit around the pump mount and offset SC ResPro 120 D5 backwards to fit accessories, tubing and fittings ontop and around TG DeltaMate GPU Block Astral making it look better
M4 16mm Screws where used to mount Bitspower BP-120RADH-BK to the PSU cage

https://www.amazon.de/dp/B09PFVGH5F Used to power the pump without turning on the system to fill the loop


You can download the first draft of a sensorpanel for 1280x800 100% window scaling screens hereI noticed that you have to disable monitoring of aquacomputer devices to get a low polling rate for per pin monitoring. You need to disable Preferences/Stability/Aquaero sensor support I've set my polling rate for the per pin monitoring to 500ms. (hammering the ec could lead to instabilities) Disable Preferences/Hardware Monitoring/SensorPanel/Pin SensorPanel to Monitor to actually pin your SensorPanel.
I've set AIDA to run a script that opens an audio file in case the gpu pins draw to much power via alerting. That way the sound doesnt stop playing until dismissed. Preferences/Hardware Monitoring/Alerting


Download: Steve
Download: Individual Components
Download: More Minecraft Stuff16,6kg without fluid 17,8kg with fluid ~12-13kg for the MO-RA extensionM.2_1 (Gen5) Debloated Windows M.2_2 (Gen4) Fedora Linux or CachyOS I did a horrible job cleaning up the cpu die after delidding I now have thermal paste all over my smds. Probably some liquid metal too I wiped the DeltaMate Backplate with an alcohol wipe (It has subtle white stripes now) Trying to screw down the PCB to the waterblock I noticed that the PCB was slightly misaligned (I had to loosen screws around the already compressed PTM on the core) After the misalignement issue I noticed that I forgot the 12VHPWR thermal pad (I had to loosen all screws again and order a new PTM Pad) I put putty on the chokes instead of the MOSFETs I ordered 100g of putty and remade it I disassembeled the loop because I had a leak The leak was at the drain port (easiest location to access)
I ordered a JST 5Pin to USB A cable because I thought the Aqua Computer D5 NEXT wouldn't run on only SATA Power I realized the external psu just wasnt powerful enough
I reused the cable for my MO-RA IV 400 Extension tho D5 didn't begin spinning The pump motor was broken and eventually repaired by aqua computer Broken CableMod Molex Cable
The rgb components were fading and the fans weren't spinning since the Aqua Computer Octo reported insufficient voltage levels
I had to drain, open the loop, and pull out the gpu to get to the molex connector the cable was plugged into (Aqua Computer farbwerk 360) I ordered random uhbr20 cables thinking they could handle 4k 240hz Had to order vesa certified cables The screen doesnt support HDCP and leads to gpu driver crashes when playing DRM content on e.g. Netflix

info_showOrphanNodes.description: Show nodes that are not connected to any other nodes.

info_showAttachments.description: Show attachments like images and PDFs as nodes in the graph.

info_allowGlobalGraph.description: Allow the user to view the global graph of all nodes.

info_allowExpand.description: Allow the user to pop-out the graph view to take up the whole screen

info_attractionForce.description: How much should linked nodes attract each other? This will make the graph appear more clustered.

info_linkLength.description: How long should the links between nodes be? The shorter the links the more connected nodes will cluster together.

info_repulsionForce.description: How much should nodes repel each other? This will make disconnected parts more spread out.

info_centralForce.description: How much should nodes be attracted to the center? This will make the graph appear more dense and circular.

info_edgePruning.description: Edges with a length above this threshold will not be rendered, however they will still contribute to the simulation. This can help large tangled graphs look more organised. Hovering over a node will still display these links.

info_minNodeRadius.description: How small should the smallest nodes be? The smaller a node is the less it will attract other nodes.

info_maxNodeRadius.description: How large should the largest nodes be? Nodes are sized by how many links they have. The larger a node is the more it will attract other nodes. This can be used to create a good grouping around the most important nodes.
